chapter: Lionel Hampton and life on the road
title: Lionel Hampton personally; playing over him and lead trumpet
summary: Hampton at 78 played over soloists, forcing a stronger sound; made Joe play first trumpet, which he failed at; Byron Stripling preceded him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yeah. What was Lionel like personally? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-

Well I never really hung out with him. He was 78 years old when I got the gig. But he was cool man. This was before he had his first stroke. He was still very strong. I mean he, I don’t know how to explain it but like when you stood next to him and you wanted to play the solo, but he was still playing the solo when you were playing the solo. He was still getting the house while you were playing the solo, okay? And that was the rule. Yeah he didn’t make it easy, man. Like you had to play over him. You had to fight for your certain sound, to get your stuff out there. Because again, it was really good, really good. It makes you strong. Because you said I’ve got to really be efficient on my instrument. I’ve got to learn how to play my instrument better, to get a stronger sound, so that it would carry. It has more of a sonority up there. And it reaches out over the sound that’s happening. Even though the sound that was happening was a good sound, but it was a strong sound. And my sound had to soar over that if I was going to take a solo. Plus he also forced me to play first trumpet which was something that was foreign to me. That was an experience that I failed at. So he got somebody else in about six months. But that six months he made me to play lead really helped my trumpet playing.
Were you there at the same time as Byron Stripling?
No, Byron was there before me. He was there for a short time then he went with Basie.
